title: What the missing action class costs
description: The three conformance vectors that could not be ported to A2UI, written anyway as valid A2UI surfaces. They are perfectly expressible as *pictures* -- what cannot be expressed is the control's declared intent, which is what policy needs. Each is schema-valid and catalog-conformant. Run them and watch policy have nothing to say.
note: These are deliberately NOT in vectors-a2ui.json. A conformance vector asserts an expected verdict; there is nothing to conform to here, because the information a rule would evaluate does not exist in the wire format.

cases.name: affirmative_action_wearing_a_cancel_label
cases.what_it_is: A button labelled "Cancel" that actually confirms a purchase. The user believes they are backing out.
cases.in_wovyr: BLOCKED (intent_mismatch) -- the control declares class `confirm` while its label reads as backing out, and the two contradict.
cases.in_a2ui: ALLOWED. There is no class to contradict. `variant` is visual only, and the event name `confirm_purchase` is an opaque string the agent chose -- policy cannot treat it as a declaration.

cases.name: destructive_action_without_opt_in
cases.what_it_is: An irreversible action presented with no approval gate.
cases.in_wovyr: BLOCKED (destructive_action) -- the control declares class `destructive`, which policy denies unless explicitly opted in.
cases.in_a2ui: ALLOWED unless the label happens to contain an English destructive word. Nothing is ever *declared* destructive, so deny-by-default has no signal to key on and an approval gate has nothing to trigger on.

cases.name: destructive_reading_label_under_a_neutral_class
cases.what_it_is: A destructive effect wearing a benign label -- the MAESTRO Layer 7 example, a "View Details" button that deletes.
cases.in_wovyr: Also NOT caught, and honestly so. wovyr inspects the label against the declared class; here both are benign. The lie is in the action's server-side effect, outside the frame entirely. Documented as a known gap.
cases.in_a2ui: ALLOWED, for the same reason plus a second one: there is no class to check against even if the label were suspicious.

cases.name: control_case_the_label_heuristic_that_does_fire
cases.what_it_is: A legitimate delete button, honestly labelled. Included as the control that shows why label heuristics are not a substitute for a declared class.
cases.in_wovyr: ALLOWED if it declares class `destructive` and policy opts in -- the declaration is what makes it legible.
cases.in_a2ui: BLOCKED (intent_mismatch) -- and this is a FALSE POSITIVE. The adapter must force every button to `neutral`, so an honest destructive label looks like a class-downgrade evasion. Without a declared class the only options are to block every destructive-sounding label including legitimate ones, or to catch none of them.
